Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zuroar 0.0.0.9000

  • New package: compressed sets of unsigned integers built on a bundled copy of CRoaring 5.4.0. In development towards the first CRAN release.

  • zuroar_info() reports the bundled CRoaring version, the SIMD paths compiled in, and the instruction sets the processor offers.

  • roar() and roar_range() build a 32-bit bitmap; roar_add() and roar_remove() return a changed copy, sharing unchanged containers; roar_contains() tests membership.

  • A bitmap is an ALTREP double vector that reads its values from the compressed form on demand and never expands behind your back: it survives saveRDS(), serialize() and a trip to a mirai or parallel worker, can be a data-frame column, and answers length(), x[[k]], x[i] (a bitmap), head(), tail(), %in%, match(), sum(), min(), max(), range(), as.integer(), as.double(), format(), print(), for and lapply(). An operation that would need the values as a plain vector, such as x[1] <- 5 or identical(x, y), is an error; compare sets with ==.

  • Errors inherit from zuroar_error, with zuroar_error_value, zuroar_error_index, zuroar_error_unsupported, zuroar_error_format and zuroar_error_memory for the specific cases.

  • Set algebra: |, &, roar_xor(), roar_andnot(), roar_union(), roar_intersect() and c() build bitmaps; ==, !=, <=, <, >= and > compare them as sets; roar_cardinality(), roar_jaccard(), roar_intersects() and roar_disjoint() answer without building one. roar_flip() flips a range.

  • x + k, x - k and roar_shift() shift every value; leaving the domain is an error unless roar_shift(drop = TRUE).

  • Ordered queries: roar_rank(), roar_select() (from 1), roar_next(), roar_prev(), roar_count() and roar_contains_range(), with inclusive ranges; roar_values() extracts a bounded number of values. roar_add() and roar_remove() take from and to for a range.

  • sort() and unique() return the bitmap; [<-, [[<-, rev() and sort(decreasing = TRUE) are errors.

  • roar_optimize(), roar_stats() and roar_size() show and tune how a bitmap is stored.

  • roar_serialize() and roar_unserialize() write and read the portable Roaring format shared with Java, Go, Rust and Python. Reading treats the bytes as untrusted: bounded, validated, and a zuroar_error_format on anything corrupt, including a corrupt .rds file. roar_serial_config() configures mirai daemons for the 64-bit class to come; 32-bit bitmaps need no configuration.

Developed by Pedro Baltazar.
